title: DatasetSplit
description:
The wire form of one dataset_splits row (0006_evidence.up.sql section 5): chapter 7 section 7.4's frozen, patient-level split. Response body of table 10.2-B row R28. THERE IS NO ROUTE THAT CREATES ONE. A split is frozen only as the second half of row R26's single seal action, because MOS-UI-130 makes the seal one operator action spanning both operations and because a freeze route would have to accept `assignments` -- and a caller that names which patients are in `test` is exactly the container MOS-TRAIN-141 refuses, with an HTTP client in front of it. The server assigns by MOS-TRAIN-112's pure function; there is no seed anywhere in this entity and 0006_evidence says in its own table comment that no seed column exists and none MUST be added.

THE WHOLE leakage_report IS PROJECTED, NOT THE VERDICT. MOS-EVID-035 stores it verbatim and MOS-EVID-036 requires every waiver reproduced in full in any ValidationReport citing the split -- 'there is no silent waiver'. More to the point on this surface: MOS-EVID-037 makes a `skipped` L4 a permanent property of the split, and a projection carrying only `frozen: true` would hide, one screen later, precisely what row R27's check battery was built to make visible.

partition_level.description: MOS-EVID-029 and MOS-STORE-293: the unit of assignment is patient_key, and dataset_split_members has PRIMARY KEY (split_id, patient_key), which makes a patient in two partitions structurally impossible. The column CHECKs the single value and this is const for the same reason: a study-level split is not a narrower option, it is the defect L1 exists to catch.

partition_patients.description: Patients per partition. MOS-TRAIN-214 adds no fourth partition and `val` is not a value; `fold` is the optional cross-validation index WITHIN a partition (MOS-EVID-030) and conflating the two is how a tuning fold becomes a test set.

assignment_method.description: MOS-TRAIN-112: assignment is a pure function evaluated once, whose output IS the manifest. A seed is an input to that one evaluation and a fact recorded here; it is never the split.

stratified_by.description: MOS-TRAIN-113's dimensions. Empty means unstratified and says so.

leakage_report.description: Stored verbatim in the column and projected verbatim here (MOS-EVID-034, MOS-EVID-035). The five top-level outcomes are the shape the ValidationReport cohort block of section 7.12.1 prints, so the report generator copies this object rather than re-rendering it into a second shape that can disagree with the first.

waivers.description: MOS-EVID-036's five required members per waiver. The console writes none and displays no control for one (MOS-UI-135), and MOS-TRAIN-115 makes a waiver on L1, L2, L3 or L5 incapable of permitting a training run in any case -- so an entry here is a governance act taken elsewhere, which this surface reports and never offers.

detail.description: Per-check hits and statistics, keyed by check id. For L4 it carries n_compared, n_skipped and the skipped series with their reasons, which is where MOS-EVID-037's 'explicit reason' lives once the split is frozen and the SealRun is history.

split_digest.description: Chapter 7's split_digest; section 12.12 spells the column manifest_digest. MOS-TRAIN-124 binds it onto every TrainingRun, which is what makes 'the run was fitted against this split' a recomputable claim rather than a reference.

leakage_outcome.description: MOS-EVID-034's four outcomes. `skipped` is not `pass`: MOS-EVID-037 requires the distinction and MOS-UI-144 requires the console to show it.
